feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iterations 0 to 5 left max_error at 0.060 to 0.061 m and line_loss_events at one per trial on the oval and s-bend, across spread (iteration 1), footprint (iteration 2), wheel track (iteration 3), wheel radius (iteration 4) and lead (iteration 5, which matched iteration 0). Iteration 6 (kp 3.0) raised the score from 26.04 to 36.31, but only on the slalom. Iteration 7 (mass 0.5 kg) lowered the score to 35.64, so mass 0.8 kg is the reference. Your +/-0.04 m, 16 mm row is the one spread not yet tested with kp 3.0. Next-race rules: (a) if line_loss_events fall below one on the oval or s-bend and max_error drops toward 0.06 m, keep the +/-0.04 m row and test kd near 0.2 to damp slalom steering_oscillation; (b) if the metrics match iteration 6 to four decimals, geometry is exhausted for this controller, so check the pipeline and move to kd or base_speed rather than another geometry change; (c) if line loss persists with max_error near 0.061 m, the row reach is not the limit, so test wheel_track 0.10 m with the new row to see whether more yaw response helps.
requested_changes: Hold sensor_positions at x = -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04 with y = 0.07 m and sensor_size 0.016 m, and keep mass 0.8 kg. This tests the wider row against the iteration-6 baseline (score 36.31).

If line_loss_events fall below one on the oval or s-bend, keep the wider row and try a lower wheel_track of 0.10 m. Iteration 3 used that value only with the narrower row, and the wider row gives the robot more tape reach to use.
If the metrics match iteration 6 to four decimals, stop geometry changes. The next lever is controller damping (kd about 0.2), which the Integrator will test, not a further row change.
